_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Spain covering Iberians/Celts, Roman Hispania, Visigothic kingdom, Moorish conquest (711-1492), Reconquista, Catholic Monarchs (Isabella+Ferdinand), Spanish Empire (conquistadors, Americas/Philippines, 'sun never sets'), Habsburgs/Bourbons, Napoleonic invasion 1808, Latin American independence, Carlist Wars, First Republic 1873, Restoration, Spanish-American War 1898, Second Republic 1931, Civil War 1936-39 (Franco vs Republicans), Franco dictatorship 1939-75, Transition/movida, democracy, EU 1986, Catalan/Basque tensions.

religion.note: Catholic Kings/Inquisition legacy; state religion until 1978 Constitution; Franco nationalcatolicismo (1939-75); rapid secularization post-Franco (church attendance ~20%, lowest in Europe); Islam expelled 1609 (Moriscos), returning via immigration (Moroccan ~800k); Jewish community (expelled 1492, Sephardic diaspora, 2015 law offered citizenship to descendants)

ethnic_groups.name: Spanish (Castilian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Castilian identity; Reconquista legacy; Spanish Empire (16th century superpower, conquistadors, Americas/Philippines); Castilian language/culture dominant; Madrid centralism; bull-fighting (controversial, banned Catalunya); flamenco (Andalusian); Catholicism historically central

ethnic_groups.name: Catalan
ethnic_groups.notes: ~7.5M in Catalunya, Valencia (Valencian variant), Balearics; distinct language/culture (Romance language, not Spanish dialect); industrialised/wealthy; independence movement (2017 referendum declared illegal, Puigdemont fled, leaders jailed, 2021 pardoned); Barcelona vs Madrid; Nueva Planta 1716 (abolished autonomy); Franco banned language; restored 1978; Estatut autonomy; sovereignty debate ongoing

ethnic_groups.name: Galician
ethnic_groups.notes: ~2.8M; Northwest (Galicia); Galician language (Portuguese-related); Celtic heritage; Atlantic identity; emigration ('gali-cian' stereotype in Americas); Santiago de Compostela pilgrimage; regionalist, not separatist

ethnic_groups.name: Basque
ethnic_groups.notes: ~2.1M; Basque Country/Navarre; Euskara language (pre-Indo-European isolate, oldest European language, origin unknown); distinct genetic profile; ETA terrorism 1959-2011 (829 killed, independence fight, ceasefire 2011, disarmed 2017); nationalist but less separatist post-ETA; strong regional identity; fueros (historic rights); industrial (Bilbao)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Moroccan (~850k, largest immigrant), Romanian (~670k), Colombian, Venezuelan (2010s crisis refugees ~500k), Ecuadorian, British (expats, Balearics/Andalusia), Chinese, Pakistani, Ukrainian (post-2022); Roma/Gitano (~750k, Andalusia, flamenco tradition, marginalized); Sephardic Jews (expelled 1492, ~50k today)

country_profile.time_zone: CET (UTC+1) / CEST (UTC+2); Canary Islands: WET (UTC+0) / WEST (UTC+1)

independence.from: Completion of Reconquista (fall of Granada, Moorish Emirate, Catholic Monarchs unified Spain); modern constitutional monarchy 1978

country_profile.notes_unique: Spanish Empire (16th-19th century, first global empire, 'sun never sets', conquistadors Cortés/Pizarro conquered Aztec/Inca, Philippines/Americas/Africa, silver from Potosí, Armada 1588 defeat, decline 18th-19th century); Spanish Civil War (1936-39, Republicans vs Nationalists/Franco, 500k dead, International Brigades, Guernica bombing Picasso, fascism vs communism/anarchism proxy, Orwell/Hemingway fought); Franco dictatorship (1939-75, Caudillo, National Catholicism, autarky, OSS/NATO member Cold War, economic miracle 1960s desarrollismo, named Juan Carlos successor); Transition (Transición 1975-82, democracy restored, 1978 Constitution, Juan Carlos key, 'Pact of Forgetting'/amnesia about Franco, regional autonomies); Catalan independence crisis (2017 referendum 40% turnout/90% yes, declared illegal, Puigdemont fled Belgium, leaders jailed, Article 155, demonstrations, political crisis); ETA terrorism (1959-2011, Basque separatists, 829 killed, ceasefire 2011, disarmed 2017); Reconquista (711-1492, 781 years Christian re-conquest of Iberia from Moors, Granada last to fall 1492); 1492 (annus mirabilis: Granada conquered, Jews expelled, Columbus discovered Americas); Alhambra (UNESCO, Granada, Moorish palace); Sagrada Família (Gaudí, unfinished 140+ years); Prado (Velázquez/Goya); Guernica (Picasso, Civil War); flamenco; siesta; tapas; paella; Cervantes (Don Quixote 1605, first modern novel); 49 UNESCO sites (3rd most)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Pedro Sánchez
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: PSOE (Socialist); PhD economics; motion of no confidence ousted Rajoy (corruption); minority government (coalition with Unidas Podemos 2020-23, now Sumar); Catalan amnesty deal 2023 (controversial, kept power with Catalan/Basque support); polarizing; longest-serving left PM since Felipe González; pro-EU; feminist 'only way' (solo sí es sí law)

head_of_state.name: King Felipe VI
head_of_state.title: King of Spain
head_of_state.notes: House of Borbón; succeeded father Juan Carlos (abdicated amid scandals); married Queen Letizia (commoner, journalist); restored monarchy's reputation; condemned Catalan independence 2017 (controversial speech); distanced from father (Juan Carlos in exile UAE since 2020, corruption allegations); constitutional monarch; popular

former_leaders.name: Mariano Rajoy
former_leaders.notes: PP (Popular Party); austerity (economic crisis, banking bailout €100B); Catalan crisis 2017 (Article 155, direct rule, referendum crackdown); Gürtel corruption (PP slush fund, motion of no confidence lost to Sánchez); conservative

former_leaders.name: José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero
former_leaders.notes: PSOE; won after Madrid train bombings March 11, 2004 (191 killed, Al-Qaeda, PP blamed ETA); withdrew Iraq troops; same-sex marriage 2005 (third country globally); financial crisis 2008 (construction bubble burst, unemployment 26%); austerity; lost 2011

former_leaders.name: José María Aznar
former_leaders.notes: PP; economic boom; Iraq War ally (Bush/Blair, unpopular in Spain); Madrid bombings March 2004 (blamed ETA falsely, lost election 3 days later); conservative, privatization

former_leaders.name: Felipe González
former_leaders.notes: PSOE; 14 years; consolidated democracy; EU entry 1986; NATO referendum 1986 (won, kept membership); Olympic 92 Barcelona/Expo Sevilla; GAL death squads scandal (anti-ETA, state terrorism, convicted); modernized Spain; social democrat

former_leaders.name: King Juan Carlos I
former_leaders.notes: Restored monarchy; Franco's chosen successor but led Transition to democracy; 1978 Constitution; 1981 coup attempt (23-F, confronted plotters on TV, heroic); modernized Spain; later scandals (elephant hunting, mistress, corruption, Swiss accounts); abdicated 2014; exile UAE 2020; controversial legacy (savior of democracy → symbol of corruption)

former_leaders.name: Francisco Franco
former_leaders.notes: Caudillo; Nationalist victory Civil War; fascist (but not full Nazi/Mussolini ally, stayed neutral WWII officially while sending Blue Division to USSR); National Catholicism; repression (100k+ executed post-war, mass graves, Historical Memory Law 2007); economic miracle 1960s (technócratas, tourism); named Juan Carlos successor (expected continuation, didn't happen); died November 1975; exhumed from Valley of the Fallen 2019 (Sánchez); still polarizes Spain

910.name: Prehistoric Iberia
910.description: The Iberian Peninsula boasts some of Europe's most spectacular prehistoric heritage, from the Altamira cave paintings to Megalithic cultures. Iberians, Celts, and Celtiberians formed the rich pre-Roman ethnic tapestry.

910.name: Roman Hispania
910.description: Rome's conquest of Hispania during the Punic Wars created one of the empire's most important provinces. Hispania produced emperors (Trajan, Hadrian, Theodosius), the philosopher Seneca, and a thoroughly Romanised civilisation.

920.name: Visigoths & Al-Andalus
920.description: The Visigothic Kingdom of Toledo unified Hispania until the devastating Umayyad conquest of 711. Al-Andalus became one of medieval Europe's most brilliant civilisations, with Córdoba as the intellectual capital of the Western world.

sub_clusters.description: The Germanic Visigoths' kingdom centred on Toledo, Reccared's conversion to Catholicism (589), the Councils of Toledo, the Visigothic legal code (Liber Iudiciorum), and the kingdom's collapse before the Umayyad invasion.

920.name: The Reconquista
920.description: The Reconquista was the centuries-long Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim rule. Beginning at Covadonga (718), it produced the kingdoms of Asturias, León, Castile, Navarre, and Aragon, and culminated in the fall of Granada (1492).

960.name: Modern Spain & European Integration
960.description: Spain's integration into Europe brought spectacular modernisation. The annus mirabilis of 1992 (Barcelona Olympics, Seville Expo, Madrid Cultural Capital) showcased a confident, democratic Spain, while ETA terrorism remained a persistent threat.

sub_clusters.name: 1992 – Annus Mirabilis
sub_clusters.description: The González era, EU structural funds transforming infrastructure, the Barcelona Olympics (1992), Seville Expo, the AVE high-speed rail, and Spain's emergence as a modern European state.

960.name: Contemporary Spain
960.description: 21st-century Spain has navigated the 2008 financial crisis, record unemployment, the end of ETA, and the dramatic Catalan independence crisis, while its democracy has matured through coalition politics and social reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Financial Crisis & Austerity
sub_clusters.description: Zapatero's social reforms, the bursting of the housing bubble (2008), the sovereign debt crisis, 27% unemployment, EU bailout of Spanish banks (2012), the Indignados/15-M movement, and the rise of Podemos and Ciudadanos.
